question:
Almost nobody reads the fine print, and one line on this screen changes what happens to everything you post. Find it before you click.

Steps:
1. Use the arrow tool to point at the line that changes what happens to your photos.
2. Place a shape on the box you would not tick yet.
3. Record your voice with 2 questions you would ask the company before agreeing.

rubric.description: No arrow or shape is placed on the board, or the voice recording is missing or blank.
Student places an arrow and a shape, but the arrow is not on line 3, OR the voice recording asks no questions.
Arrow points to line 3 AND a shape is on the "I agree" box AND the voice recording asks at least 2 questions about consent, payment, or what exactly will be used.
Meets all of the above AND the voice recording explains that agreeing gives the company something of value (the posts) in exchange for the service.

whiteboard_starter_image_alt_text: "You are signing up for a photo app." A sign-up screen titled "Join PicShare" with email and password fields and four numbered lines of fine print: 1, "You must be 13 or older to sign up."; 2, "We may send you updates about new features."; 3, "Anything you post can be used to train our AI products. You will not be paid."; and 4, "We may change these terms at any time." Below the fine print are an empty checkbox labeled "I agree to everything above" and a "Sign up" button.
